incident-bot: INCIDENT — prod-us-east-1: KV cache growth + tail latency spike observed on spec-decode flows. kv_cache_size ↑ 20x, 95p latency baseline 3.2s -> 18s. paging oncall.

Anna (oncall): acked. Paging Alex and Mira. Putting a priority page on this — looks widespread across several inference pods.

Alex (eng-runtime): I can see continuous-batching escalated to enormous batch sizes for long context requests on models with speculative decoding enabled. Lots of duplicate KV entries — suspect draft vs commit key divergence in the spec-decode path (draft keys getting written but never normalized to the final key). That plus autoscaling batching = cache blowup and perf cliff.

Mira (eng-ml): we shipped a speculative-draft optimization yesterday that changed key prefixing to include token-level draft ids. If commit path didn't atomically replace or collapse drafts, you can get N entries per speculative branch.

Thomas (sre): any 5xx/503 customer-facing errors? scope of impact?

Jess (customer-success): CS: five Dedicated customers reported elevated latencies and some missing responses (timeouts) over the last ~30m. One large customer (acct-42) reported degraded UX for search and reranking. No mass 5xx but lots of timeouts and retries increased cost.

Alex (eng-runtime): Proposed immediate mitigations:
- disable speculative decoding feature-flag for prod model group
- force fixed max batch size (temp hotfix) to prevent runaway batching (suggest MAX_BATCH=32)
- purge duplicated KV entries on affected nodes / restart kvcache pods if necessary

Mira (eng-ml): agree. Disabling speculative draft KV should stop new duplicates from being created. We'll need to follow up to coalesce existing keys or trigger a safe purge.

Alex (eng-runtime): commands I'm going to run (rolling changes):
```
# disable speculative draft kv feature flag in control plane
curl -X POST https://console.internal/api/flags -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' -d '{"flag":"speculative_draft_kv","value":false,"scope":"prod"}'

# set fixed max batch env var for runtime deployment
kubectl -n inference set env deployment/serve-runtime MAX_BATCH=32

# purge kvcache entries on nodes showing highest growth (example)
kubectl -n inference exec deploy/kvcache-0 -- /app/bin/kvctl purge --prefix speculative_ --force
```

deploy-bot: rollout started for deploy/serve-runtime (image: serve-runtime:v2026-11-hotfix) — 6/6 pods updated. Feature-flag change applied to control plane.

Anna (oncall): I applied the flag change in console and verified control plane reports flag=false in prod. Rolling restart of runtime in progress.

Alex (eng-runtime): hotfix pushed to revert continuous-batching heuristic that allowed unbounded growth. Rolling restart complete for the runtime. Monitoring metrics now.

Thomas (sre): metrics update — looking at prometheus: kv_cache_size trending down from peak, 95p latency dropping. Still some tail spikes on node-3.

~7m later~
Alex (eng-runtime): 95p latency trending back to ~1.8s, overall token cost rate normalized, kv_cache_size back to ~1.1x baseline. Purge reduced speculative-prefixed keys by ~92% on affected pods.

Jess (customer-success): CS: three of the five affected customers reported recovered UX. acct-42 still seeing slowest requests occasionally — filed support case and escalated infra.

Mira (eng-ml): need postmortem action items: 1) ensure speculative draft keys are normalized atomically on commit; 2) add regression tests for draft->commit key collapse under high concurrency; 3) add metric: speculative-draft-key-count and alert threshold; 4) document safe coalescing/purge procedure.

Alex (eng-runtime): root-cause (initial): speculative-draft key prefixes were introduced without an atomic promotion to final commit key; races + continuous batching allowed many speculative branches to be materialized in KV. Autoscaling batch heuristics aggravated the problem by increasing batch size when latency decreased, creating an amplification feedback loop.

Anna (oncall): handing off to Alex for postmortem write-up and Mira for ML follow-up on the speculative design. Thomas to own infra runbook updates (purge + rolling restart checklist). Jess to follow up with customers and close support cases.

Alex (eng-runtime): I'll draft a postmortem and include timeline + mitigation steps + code pointers. Early ETA: PR + initial postmortem draft in 3h.

Anna (oncall): oncall cleared for now but keep watching for 1h. If any residual errors for acct-42 persist, page immediately.

Jess (customer-success): will send interim status to affected customers and flag any SLA concerns.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — mitigation applied. Next steps: postmortem + alerts + regression tests.

Thomas (sre): created infra ticket INFRA-1423 for purge runbook and MAX_BATCH guardrails.

Alex (eng-runtime): quick note for postmortem: include snippet of the key normalization bug (diff) and the batching heuristic config that allowed growth. Also include the commands used (above) and the roll timings.

Mira (eng-ml): we'll add an ML test harness to simulate speculative branches at scale before flipping feature flags.

Anna (oncall): thanks team. Handoff complete. :white_check_mark:
